Cc: security@oasishc.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Consolidated subprocessor snapshot + evidence for SIG/SOC2 review

Hi Ben,

We're kicking off a SIG/SOC2 refresh and procurement needs a consolidated snapshot of Redwood's current subprocessor roster with the following details for each: residency (region/country), KMS custody/residency, data access scope, and pointer to the most recent evidence (SOC2 report, CAIQ responses, or SIG attachments).

Can you provide a single CSV (or equivalent) plus an index PDF that maps to artifact locations? Ideal delivery by EOD next Wednesday (2027-04-14) — we can take a phased delivery if needed.

Also please note any items with export-control or residency exceptions up front. We may need a short provenance note for KMS custodianship.

Thanks — Nora

Subject: Re: Request: Consolidated subprocessor snapshot + evidence for SIG/SOC2 review

Nora — thanks for the clear ask. We'll compile a consolidated subprocessor snapshot and an evidence index. Proposed plan: 

1) Draft CSV (roster + residency + KMS owner + minimal access scope) delivered by 2027-04-06 EOD for your triage.
2) Evidence index (PDF) with direct links or Drive paths to SOC2/SIG/CAIQ artifacts by 2027-04-08.
3) Karthik will provide a short KMS provenance note and list of any residency exceptions by 2027-04-09.

Marissa is pulling the roster export and will attach the initial CSV. Karthik — can you confirm the cadence above works on your side?

If you want us to redact anything sensitive (IPs, contract numbers) we can provide redacted and unredacted versions under an NDA — let us know.

Ben

Ben / Nora — attaching the first-pass artifacts. See attachments:
- subprocessor_inventory_20270405.csv (roster columns: vendor, service, country, region, data_types, kms_owner, contract_start, contract_end, notes)
- sig_evidence_index_20270405.pdf (index mapping to Drive paths; includes SOC2 report dates where applicable)

Notes / caveats:
- Residency populated from our vendor master; for three smaller contractors we include 'regional' rather than specific country pending vendor confirmation.
- KMS ownership column lists the Redwood-managed key identifier when applicable; where vendor manages keys we note that as vendor_kms.
- We've flagged 4 vendors with residency exceptions for EU-data processing — see notes column.

Attachment stubs: subprocessor_inventory_20270405.csv (csv), sig_evidence_index_20270405.pdf (pdf)

If you need a combined redacted copy for procurement distribution I can produce one next. Karthik — I left placeholders where you indicated you would add the provenance notes.

—Marissa

Adding the KMS and provenance details — quick summary (will drop a short note as kms_provenance_note.txt in the Drive):

- Redwood keys: primary key rings for tokenization and telemetry are resident in us-west-2 (AWS KMS); key IDs listed in the CSV are internal references, not raw key material.
- Vendor-managed keys: marked vendor_kms in CSV. For those vendors we include the custody model and contract clause pointer in the PDF index.
- Ephemeral access: where we provide ephemeral encryption/decryption access (e.g., secure logging pipelines), we document the TTL and access grants in the provenance note.
- Export-control flags: mentioned in the CSV notes column for the three EU-processing vendors. We'll follow up if any export licensing paperwork is required.

Action items:
- Marissa: please upload the two artifacts to the Drive folder and add me to the index so I can attach kms_provenance_note.txt.
- Ben / Nora: once you confirm the timeline is acceptable, we'll finalize the full artifact set and provide a redacted export if procurement requires it.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Inference Security | Redwood Inference
